summary: The 6 tier C freeholds of the Ember Lands: the lord's hall or the freeholders' moot, furnace lands, the shadow of Nafeher, storm coasts, a client crown or a ward of Mirolon, the Houses, war and the lifting of the storm. Modules L1 to L10.

lords_writ.name: The Lord's Writ
lords_writ.desc: The lord's seal is on every deed and every summons, and the bailiffs carry his word to the farthest farmstead.

freeholders_moot.name: The Freeholders' Moot
freeholders_moot.desc: Each farm sends one voice, and the moot decides by the show of hands.

essence_vents_spirit.name: The Essence Vents
essence_vents_spirit.desc: Warm essence is caught from the vents in sealed cisterns and carried to the forges.

southern_stone.name: Stone of the South
southern_stone.desc: Pale stone cut from the hills builds houses, walls and bridges that last.

walls_hold.name: The Walls Hold
walls_hold.desc: Every stone of the wall was laid by a freeholder who knew he would stand behind it.

storm_shelter.name: The Storm Shelters Us
storm_shelter.desc: The storms that wreck strangers on the reefs keep the coast safe from landings.

quiet_hearts_spirit.name: Quiet Hearts
quiet_hearts_spirit.desc: The safest thing to feel is nothing, and the safest thing to say is less.

lake_trade_spirit.name: Trade with the Lake Towns
lake_trade_spirit.desc: Barges bring grain and timber down from the north and carry iron and ember-glass back.

one_watch_spirit.name: One Watch
one_watch_spirit.desc: The wardens' signal-fires and the freehold's beacons form one chain, and the watch does not sleep.

houses_of_healing_spirit.name: Houses of Healing
houses_of_healing_spirit.desc: Clean beds, warm broth and scribes who teach the children their letters.

own_healers.name: Our Own Healers
own_healers.desc: The leeches and midwives form a guild of their own and ask nothing of strangers.

night_cults.name: The Night Cults
night_cults.desc: Black-robed congregations sing to the dark in cellars, and the by-day silence is deeper for it.

wardens_way.name: The Wardens' Way
wardens_way.desc: Every village keeps a watch-bell, and every bell has a rope within a child's reach.

warlords_rule.name: A Warlord's Rule
warlords_rule.desc: One strong man holds the hall by the strength of his household, and his laws are short.

hold_the_walls_spirit.name: Hold the Walls
hold_the_walls_spirit.desc: Farmers become sentries and wagons become barricades.

freehold_hall.title: The Hall of [ROOT.GetName]
freehold_hall.desc: The great doors of the hall stand open, and the benches fill from the front. The lord of the house waits at one end of the board and the elder of the freeholders at the other, and the whole hall waits to see who rises first.

rumours_from_nafeher.title: The Storm over Nafeher
rumours_from_nafeher.desc: A pedlar from the south tells the hall that the storms over Nafeher have not lifted in a year. Riders from there buy iron and ask no prices, and the pedlar does not like the way they look at the road north.

freehold_offers_tribute.title: Tribute from [FROM.GetName]
freehold_offers_tribute.desc: A line of wagons from [FROM.GetName] waits at the southern gate, heavy with grain and iron. Its steward asks for nothing but that the old quiet be kept between the freehold and Nafeher.

freehold_offers_friendship.title: Friendship from [FROM.GetName]
freehold_offers_friendship.desc: Envoys of [FROM.GetName] stand in the wardens' hall, in their best cloaks, and ask for a place at the table of the free south. They bring no tribute, only a hand held out.

houses_come_south.title: The Houses Come South
houses_come_south.desc: Healers and scribes of the Houses of the First Light stand at the gate of [ROOT.GetName]. They ask leave to open a house of healing, and they bring bread, herbs and little else.

the_storm_lifts.title: The Storm Lifts
the_storm_lifts.desc: The storms over Nafeher thin. What remains of its master, no one living can say.

focuses.name: The Freehold of [ROOT.GetName]
focuses.desc: Fields, farmsteads and a few walled towns make up [ROOT.GetName], and every man who owns a plough has a say in what is done. The hall is opened, the bell is rung, and the freeholders gather to settle who will lead them through the storm years.

focuses.name: The Lord's Hall
focuses.desc: The oldest family of [ROOT.GetName] holds the great hall and keeps its keys. Its lord sits at the head of the board, hears every petition and settles it before the soup is cold.

focuses.name: The Free Folk
focuses.desc: The yeomen of [ROOT.GetName] have never bent the knee to a lord who did not first buy their grain. They meet in the churchyard and keep a muster-roll in an oak chest.

focuses.name: The Lord's Writ
focuses.desc: The lord's seal is pressed to every deed and every summons, and the bailiffs carry his writ to the farthest farmstead. Order is quick and plain, and few dare answer back.

focuses.name: The Freeholders' Moot
focuses.desc: Each farm of [ROOT.GetName] sends one voice to the moot, and the moot decides by the show of hands. It is slow, loud and fair, and nobody who has sat in it will ever call it a mere custom.

focuses.name: The Freehold Endures
focuses.desc: Whatever rules [ROOT.GetName], its people have agreed that it will go on. Barns are mended, fences are walked and the old grudges are kept for a quieter year.

focuses.name: Furnace Lands
focuses.desc: South of the old border the earth is hot to the touch, and iron comes out of the hills almost clean. [ROOT.GetName] builds its first smelting-hall among the vents and puts a roof over the heat.

focuses.name: The Essence Vents
focuses.desc: Where the ground breathes out a thick, warm essence, the folk of [ROOT.GetName] have put up sealed cisterns and learned to catch it. It lights lamps, tempers blades and, mixed with the right salts, drives a forge twice as hot.

focuses.name: Cistern Roads
focuses.desc: In a land where rain is rare, every road runs from one cistern to the next. [ROOT.GetName] lays new stone beside the old and puts a water-house at every league.

focuses.name: Ash Forges
focuses.desc: Forges burn night and day beside the vents, and their ash is carted to the fields to sweeten the soil. The swords that come out of them are grey, hard and slightly warm to the touch.

focuses.name: Stone of the South
focuses.desc: Pale quarries are opened in the hills, and the cut stone is rafted down the dry river-beds in flood season. Houses, walls and bridges rise from them, and [ROOT.GetName] looks sturdier by the year.

focuses.name: The Furnace Provides
focuses.desc: Between the vents and the quarries, [ROOT.GetName] has all it needs to build. Guilds rise, apprentices multiply and the first merchant-barons begin to dream of ships.

focuses.name: The Storm over Nafeher
focuses.desc: The storms over Nafeher have not lifted in a year, and the folk of [ROOT.GetName] watch the southern sky with unease. Riders from the south buy iron and ask no prices, which is more worrying than a bad bargain.

focuses.name: Keep the Old Quiet
focuses.desc: The quiet that has lain between Nafeher and the freeholds is older than any treaty. [ROOT.GetName] sends a gift of grain and iron, and asks nothing but that the quiet go on.

focuses.name: The Wardens' Friend
focuses.desc: Mirolon's wardens have watched the south for generations, and a freehold that stands beside them is no longer alone. [ROOT.GetName] sends a delegation with an offer of friendship.

focuses.name: Behind Our Walls
focuses.desc: Neither tribute nor friendship: [ROOT.GetName] will keep itself to itself and trust to stone. Masons fill the ditches, raise the gatehouses and set a watch on every road.

focuses.name: The Quiet Kept
focuses.desc: Nafeher has taken the gift and has sent no riders. The folk of [ROOT.GetName] dare to breathe again, and the merchants begin to trade on the southern roads.

focuses.name: Join the Warden League
focuses.desc: Mirolon has raised its banner over a league of the free south, and [ROOT.GetName] has been asked to stand beneath it. The terms are simple: a watch on the passes and a seat at the wardens' table.

focuses.name: The Walls Hold
focuses.desc: Every stone of the new wall has been laid by a freeholder who knows he will stand behind it. When the south tests it, the wall will remember that.

focuses.name: A Harbour on the Storm Coast
focuses.desc: The coast is cursed with storms that wreck foreign ships on its reefs, but the steersmen of [ROOT.GetName] know every rock. A sheltered quay is dug into a cove, and a watch-house is raised on the cliff above.

focuses.name: Storm-Wise Sailors
focuses.desc: Sailors from [ROOT.GetName] learn to read a storm by the colour of the evening sky and the taste of the wind. They sail when others hide and return when others have been wrecked.

focuses.name: Cliff Beacons
focuses.desc: Fires burn on the headlands from dusk to dawn, and keepers sleep in stone huts beside them. A ship that sees the beacons knows where the reefs are, and a raider that sees them knows he has been seen.

focuses.name: The Storm Shelters Us
focuses.desc: The same storms that wreck strangers keep the coast of [ROOT.GetName] safe from landings. The folk say the sea itself is on their side, and the sailors have stopped arguing.

focuses.name: A Client Crown
focuses.desc: The banner of Nafeher flies over the hall of [ROOT.GetName], and its lord holds his seat at the pleasure of another. The people are ordered to be quiet and, for the most part, are.

focuses.name: Tribute to Nafeher
focuses.desc: Each season a line of wagons leaves [ROOT.GetName] for the south, heavy with grain, hides and silver. The drivers are sworn never to speak of what they see at the other end.

focuses.name: Quiet Hearts
focuses.desc: The people of [ROOT.GetName] have learned that the safest thing to feel is nothing, and the safest thing to say is less. Quarrels end before they begin, and the gaols stand empty.

focuses.name: Serve the Dark Crown
focuses.desc: The lord of [ROOT.GetName] gives up all pretence and serves the crown of Nafeher as a loyal retainer. The old customs fall away one by one, and the hall is hung with black.

focuses.name: Wait for the Storm to Pass
focuses.desc: The elders of [ROOT.GetName] say that every storm ends and that a client crown is only a crown that waits. They keep the old laws in cellars, teach them to the children and bide their time.

focuses.name: The Crown Remembers
focuses.desc: With the master of Nafeher silent, the crown of [ROOT.GetName] remembers that it was a crown before it was a client. Its seal is brought out of the strongbox and polished.

focuses.name: Under the Wardens' Banner
focuses.desc: The banner of Mirolon's wardens flies on the tower of [ROOT.GetName], and the garrison wears the grey cloak. The freehold keeps its laws, and the wardens keep the watch.

focuses.name: Levies for the Passes
focuses.desc: Young men of [ROOT.GetName] go north to hold the mountain passes of Mirolon under the grey cloak. They are fed, paid and drilled by wardens who have held those passes for generations.

focuses.name: Trade with the Lake Towns
focuses.desc: Barges from the northern lakes bring grain, salt fish and cut timber down to [ROOT.GetName], and return with iron and ember-glass. Lake towns learn to love the south, and the south learns to love their coin.

focuses.name: One Watch
focuses.desc: The wardens' signal-fires and the freehold's beacons are joined in one chain, and a watcher on a hill of [ROOT.GetName] can send word to Mirolon in an hour. There is one watch now, and it does not sleep.

focuses.name: The Houses Come South
focuses.desc: Healers and scribes in white-trimmed robes arrive at the gates of [ROOT.GetName], carrying herbs, ledgers and letters of introduction. They ask for nothing but leave to open a house.

focuses.name: Houses of Healing
focuses.desc: A house of healing opens on the market square: clean beds, warm broth and scribes who teach the children their letters. The poor of [ROOT.GetName] bless it, and the lord is not sure why he feels uneasy.

focuses.name: Our Own Healers
focuses.desc: The leeches and midwives of [ROOT.GetName] form a guild of their own and refuse the strangers' offer. Their medicine is slower and less gentle, but it asks no one for anything.

focuses.name: The Night Cults
focuses.desc: When the sun goes down over [ROOT.GetName], black-robed congregations meet in cellars and old crypts to sing to the dark. By day they pay their taxes and say nothing.

focuses.name: The Wardens' Way
focuses.desc: The wardens of Mirolon teach that a free people keeps its own watch, and [ROOT.GetName] takes the lesson to heart. Every village has a watch-bell, and every watch-bell has a rope within a child's reach.

focuses.name: A Warlord's Rule
focuses.desc: One strong man has taken the hall of [ROOT.GetName] and holds it by the strength of his household. His laws are short, his punishments are quick and his captains have never lost a quarrel.

focuses.name: [ROOT.GetName] at War
focuses.desc: The beacons are lit, the bell is rung and every house sends its sons to the muster-field. Whatever this war is, [ROOT.GetName] has not chosen it, and will not forget who did.

focuses.name: Hold the Walls
focuses.desc: Farmers become sentries, and wagons become barricades. The walls of the freehold are lined with archers, and the gate is held by a man who has sworn not to leave it.

focuses.name: The Freeholders Rise
focuses.desc: Where the enemy has taken a farm or a mill, the freeholders of [ROOT.GetName] take it back by night. They have no banners, no drill and no mercy for those who burned their barns.

focuses.name: The Freehold Returns
focuses.desc: The last foe has gone, and the freeholders come home to ruined barns and trampled fields. They rebuild, because there is nothing else to do and no one else to do it.

focuses.name: The Storm Lifts
focuses.desc: The storms over Nafeher thin. What remains of its master, no one living can say.

focuses.name: The Exiles Return
focuses.desc: Families who fled the south in the dark years come home along the roads of Mirolon, thin, travel-stained and unbowed. [ROOT.GetName] gives them bread, beds and a place at the fire.

focuses.name: Free of Nafeher
focuses.desc: No rider has come from the south in months, and the tribute wagons stand empty in the yard. The lord of [ROOT.GetName] declares the old debts ended, and nobody answers him back.

focuses.name: The South Breathes
focuses.desc: Fields are sown that lay fallow for a generation, and the roads of [ROOT.GetName] fill with carts. The sky over the south is merely cloudy now, and people look up at it without flinching.
